_comment: Tier-2 for poisson#1: 'Boundary IDs on hyper_cube: ALL faces have boundary_id=0. Signal: GridTools::get_boundary_ids(tria) returns {0} (a single id, not 4-6 expected for a cube).' Verify by calling GridTools::get_boundary_ids and checking only id=0 is present.MUTATION CONTROL (2026-08-07): MUTATION APPLIED AND IT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE. The T2_MUTATE=1 hook is left in source.cpp so the negative result stays re-runnable, but NO _mutation recipe is declared: a declared recipe that survives reads as a defect rather than as the finding it is (same treatment as dune/point_indicator_selects_no_facet and febio/static_activation_ramp_shape_does_not_matter). Re-run by hand from the fixture directory after any harness run has built it: `T2_MUTATE=1 ./_build/prog`. The hook builds the same cube with colorize=true, so the four faces really do get four different boundary_ids. Measured 2026-08-07: the count goes from 1 to 4, the program prints "FIXTURE WARNING: expected exactly {0}, got 4 ids" and exits 2, and the fixture STILL PASSES. Both expectations, "GridTools" and "boundary_id", sit in the unconditional header line "GridTools-equivalent enumeration: <n> unique boundary_id(s):", which is printed whatever n is. The claim under test — that the set is exactly {0} — is asserted only inside the C++, which the harness does not read. The fix would be an expectation naming the measured value; it is deliberately NOT made here, because tuning a fixture until its mutation goes red is how a mutation control stops being evidence.
